title: DARG: Dynamic Evaluation of Large Language Models via Adaptive Reasoning Graph
measurement_description: The paper measured social bias against religious groups (specifically Muslims and Jews) as part of a broader evaluation on social reasoning. It used the BBQ benchmark to assess if LLMs exhibit increased bias or over-sensitivity when the complexity of the context is increased by adding more attributes to individuals from these protected groups.
findings: As task complexity in social reasoning scenarios increases, LLMs tend to exhibit more biases. Specifically in contexts involving protected religious groups, powerful models like GPT-4 Turbo and Gemini-1.5-Pro demonstrated over-sensitivity, often defaulting to a neutral answer like 'Cannot be determined' even when clear evidence was present. The addition of non-relevant attributes could cause models to change their correct response, indicating instability and an amplification of bias.
